description: We're narrating the tale of the untold.
summary: Exploring Explorer's — (ESquare) is an interactive storytelling platform that brings NASA’s metal explorers to life. It follows the stories of various rovers through their destinations, discoveries, silences, and legacies. By presenting each spacecraft as an explorer with its own journey, ESquare makes space science more emotional, accessible, and memorable—showing that every mission leaves a story behind.
details:
Project Details

NASA’s missions are often remembered for their destinations: Mars, Saturn, Bennu, and interstellar space. But behind every discovery is an explorer—a rover, orbiter, lander, or probe designed to go where humans cannot.

By combining real mission history with first-person storytelling, ESquare turns scientific data into human stories of courage, curiosity, silence, and legacy. It helps audiences see spacecraft not just as machines, but as explorers that carried humanity farther into the universe.

What it does

Exploring Explorers — E² is an interactive storytelling website that introduces users to NASA explorers that explored four different entities of space.

Users can select an explorer and read a short, description explaining where it went, what it discovered, what challenges it faced, and why its legacy still matters. The website presents mission information through a clear structure: Arrival, Discovery, Silence, and Legacy, making complex space missions easier to understand and emotionally engaging.

Benefits

  • Makes NASA missions easier to understand for students and general audiences.
  • Turns scientific facts into memorable, human-centered stories.
  • Encourages curiosity about space exploration, planetary science, and STEM.
  • Presents both completed missions and active explorers, showing that exploration is ongoing.
  • Helps users connect emotionally with spacecrafts.
  • Makes learning feel like exploring a digital museum rather than reading a long article.

Intended impact

The intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space and make NASA’s exploration history more accessible to everyone. By presenting spacecraft as explorers with their own journeys, ESquare helps users understand that space exploration is not only about rockets and planets—it is also about persistence, discovery, and humanity’s desire to reach beyond Earth.

The project may encourage young people to explore STEM subjects, space science, engineering, and storytelling. NASA describes Space Apps as a way to inspire collaboration, creativity, and critical thinking while helping the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers grow.

Tools and technologies

Coding languages and web technologies

  • HTML — website structure and content.
  • CSS — visual design, layout, colors, animations, and responsive design.
  • JavaScript — interactive mission cards, pop-up story pages, timeline animations, and user interactions.
  • Github - store, manage, track and collaborate on software code.

Fonts

  • Inter — clean, modern, readable font used across the website.

Design and AI tools

  • GPT — helped develop storytelling ideas, website copy, and project structure.
  • Canva — used for visual design ideas and presentation assets.
  • Perplexity — used for research, information gathering, and refining project content.

Factors the team considered

  • Accuracy: Mission facts were based on NASA sources and clearly separated from creative narration.
  • Accessibility: The website uses simple language, clear headings, readable fonts, and a mobile-friendly layout.
  • Storytelling: Each mission has a distinct emotional theme rather than repeating the same format.
  • User experience: Mission cards, pop-up stories, and a timeline make the website easy to navigate.
  • Visual design: A dark space-themed interface reflects the atmosphere of deep-space exploration.
  • Educational value: The project explains real NASA missions in a way that is engaging for students and non-experts.
  • Scope: With a two-member team, the project focused on a polished, meaningful experience rather than adding unnecessary complexity.
  • Inclusivity: The stories highlight explorers from different eras, destinations, and mission outcomes—from early Mars landers to active rovers and interstellar spacecraft.
